source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 9, Schedule 1 Line 43; PDF page 10 ('Tier 1 and Tier 2 railroad retirement benefits are fully exempt'); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 25,000.00 + Tier 1/Tier 2 railroad retirement 30,000.00 = 55,000.00. Federal taxable income = 55,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 37,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 55,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 55,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 43 Tier 1 and Tier 2 railroad retirement: fully exempt, no income test -> 30,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 30,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 30,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 55,000.00 - 30,000.00 = 25,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 25,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 25,000.00 is not more than 30,000.00, exemption 15,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 25,000.00 - 15,000.00 = 10,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 10,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 = 200.00 = 200.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 25,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 200.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.35 (Connecticut AGI 25,000.00 is in the band more than 22,300.00); Line 9 = 200.00 x 0.35 = 70.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 200.00 - 70.00 = 130.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Railroad retirement reported on federal Form 1040 Line 5b; subtracted on Line 43, not in the Line 48b worksheet.
